{{Recipe}}

'''Abacha mmiri''' (literally "water cassava flakes"), also known as '''bobozee''', is a Nigerian snack prepared from cassava.

==Ingredients==
*1 tuber of [[Cookbook:Cassava|cassava]]
* 1–2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]], to taste
*½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] fresh [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]] pieces
*¼ cup [[Cookbook:Oil Palm Fruit|palm kernel]]
*¼ cup roasted [[Cookbook:Groundnut|groundnuts]]

==Procedure==
#Peel the cassava, then cut into [[Cookbook:Slicing|slices]] 1 cm thick. Rinse well.
#[[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] the cassava in a large pot of water until cooked through.
#Soak the cooked cassava in fresh water overnight. The next day, drain away any remaining water and rinse the cassava well.
#Season the cassava to taste with the salt.
#Serve the cassava with the coconut, palm kernel, and roasted groundnut.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* The cassava is rinsed after soaking to remove the sour taste that develops.
